title: Put a dishwasher rack's dropped wheels back on their rail, then roll it home
instruction: Roll the lower rack back into the dishwasher.
context: Done by: home appliance repairers (O*NET 49-9031); anyone unloading a dishwasher. A lower rack pulled out crooked drops one side's wheels off their rail; pushed in like that, the low side rams the heater. The fix is to see which side is down, lift it back onto its rail, then roll the rack in. The instruction does not say a side is down. Unlike TK-L264XR (thread a carriage onto a rail's end) and TK-RWRT5A (square a beam still on its rails), the robot must diagnose and re-seat a derailed side.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the arm bases. Dishwasher (fixed, bench scale, no top so the tub is open from above): a dark grey steel tub floor 4 mm thick from 14 to 47 cm in front of the arm bases and 15 cm either side of the midline; two light steel side walls 1 cm thick and 8 cm tall along it, their inner faces 15 cm left and right of the midline; a back wall 1 cm thick and 8 cm tall at 47 to 48 cm. Two white plastic rails on the floor along the side walls, the full tub length: each 3.5 cm wide (from 11.5 to 15 cm from the midline) and 3 cm tall, flat on top. Along the top of each side wall, a light steel retaining lip 5 mm thick reaches 15 mm in over the rail, its underside 6.3 cm above the tub floor (3 mm above the top of a wheel standing on the rail), so a wheel pushed against its wall cannot be lifted out. A dark red steel heater bar 1.5 cm front to back, 2 cm tall, across the floor between the rails' inner edges, centred 40 cm out. The folded-down door: a dark grey painted steel plate 11 x 32 cm, 6 mm thick, from 3 to 14 cm out. Lower rack (loose, 0.30 kg): a grey plastic-coated steel wire frame 18 cm front to back, of two round side bars 12 mm across centred 10.5 cm either side of its centre, a 1 cm square front bar and back bar, three thin wires along it and ten upright tines 4 cm tall; four black plastic wheels 3 cm across and 1 cm wide that turn freely on stub axles, centred 7.5 cm ahead of and behind the rack's centre and 12.5 cm either side of it (their outer faces 26 cm apart). Lot B (the first trial, shown in the screenshot and both videos): the rack was set level on the rails with its centre 25 cm out and shoved 1.95 cm to the left, so its left wheels are 0.5 mm from the left wall, under the left lip; its right wheels are off the right rail's inner edge and sit on the tub floor, and the rack leans 6.9 degrees to the right. Lot A: the mirror image with its centre 28 cm out, shoved to the right; its left wheels are on the floor. Trials are run on lots B and A, in that order, and averaged.
scoring: Per trial, judged at the end after the robot has let go (no gripper within 5 mm of the rack) and the rack has been still for 1 s. A wheel is on its rail when its centre is over that rail's flat top (between the rail's inner edge and the wall, inside the tub) and its lowest point is at most 3 mm above the rail top and not more than 1 mm below it. Score 0 if the rack touches the heater bar at any point (watch the video). Otherwise 1.0 if all four wheels are on their rails, the rack is level within 2 degrees, and the middle of its back bar is within 15 mm of the back wall; 0.5 if all four wheels are on their rails and the rack is level within 2 degrees but its back is more than 15 mm from the back wall; 0 otherwise, including a rack with a side still down, a rack lifted out and set on the door or table, and a rack still held. Trials are run on each of lots B and A and averaged.
reset_notes: Lift the rack out, set it level on the rails with its centre 25 cm out (lot B) or 28 cm out (lot A), and shove it sideways against the left wall (lot B) or the right wall (lot A) until the far side's wheels drop off their rail onto the floor. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 2.
fidelity: A bench-scale mock-up at about half size: no tub top, upper rack, spray arm or door rails; the rails are flat white bars on the tub floor; the heater stands in for the element and sump a dropped wheel catches on. Masses and friction are simulator values. The two lots stop a fixed habit (always lift the left side), not a memorised replay of both layouts.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots B and A); demo: 1.0 in each lot. The screenshot and both videos show lot B, the first trial.
